$comment: Terminology policy for the Bangla content. `preferred` is enforced by tools/check-terms.mjs and applied by the Stage 6 sweep: the left side is what lesson prose should say, the right side is the variant to avoid. `protected` lists the strings a sweep must never rewrite even when a `preferred` key is a substring of them -- Bangla is agglutinative, so a naive replace turns পাঠানো ("to send") into লেসনানো. See CONTRIBUTING.md. SCOPE: the policy applies to lesson BODY prose, frontmatter `description`, mermaid node labels and component prose. It does NOT apply to navigation -- lesson titles (frontmatter `title`, and the same strings in src/lib/lessons.ts) and the five domain labels in src/lib/domains.ts stay Bangla by decision, so the sweep and the checker both skip `title:`/`titleEn:` lines and src/lib/domains.ts.

policy.phrases-latin: Multi-word API concept phrases stay Latin: conversation history, tool call, iteration cap, system prompt.
policy.nouns-bangla: General technical nouns keep their Bangla transliteration: টুল, এজেন্ট, কনটেক্সট, প্রম্পট, ডেভেলপার.
policy.identifiers-latin: Code identifiers are never transliterated: stop_reason, tool_use, tool_choice, PreToolUse, CLAUDE.md, fork_session.

knownGaps.note: Both idiomatic and already user-visible (bn-BD.json, Attribution.astro); not an error, so not swept.
Different parts of speech -- কনফিগার করুন is the verb, কনফিগারেশন the noun. Both correct.
